chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:
I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) spread the soil upon the deceased, so he held it for a while in his hand, then spread it, and he did not exceed three handfuls.

He said, so I asked him about that, and he said: O Umar! I was saying: 'Belief in You and confirmation of Your Resurrection. This is what Allah and His Messenger promised,' up to His words, 'submission'.
Thus was what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do, and by it the Sunnah has flowed.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed number of handfuls of soil to spread on the deceased during burial according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific Sunnah of the Prophet and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in burial rites, where soil is spread in three handfuls while reciting verses affirming faith in resurrection and submission. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on emulating the Prophet’s physical actions as a tangible expression of theological belief in the Hereafter. The act serves as a practical demonstration of trust in the divine promise, linking ritual precision with spiritual conviction.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Umar Bin Azina who said,

‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> spread the soil upon the decease. So he<sup>asws</sup> withheld it for a while in his<sup>asws</sup> hand, then spread it, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not increased upon three handfulls.

So I asked himasws about that, and heasws said: ‘O Umar! Iasws was saying: ‘Iasws believe in Youazwj, and ratify Yourazwj Resurrection. [33:22] This is what Allah and His Rasool promised us, and Allah and His Rasool spoke the truth up to Hisazwj Words (and it only increased them in faith and) submission’.
This what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to do, and by it has the Sunnah flowed’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah who has said the following: “I saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, fill soil in the grave of a deceased.
He held it (soil) in his hand for a while then tossed it in the grave and did not do more than three handfuls.

I asked him about it and he replied, ‘O ‘Umar I was saying, “It is out of faith in You (O Allah), and an acknowledgement of Your resurrecting (people). This is what Allah and His Messenger have promised us.
Allah and His Messenger are truthful. This has only increased our faith and acceptance.” This is how the Messenger of Allah would do and thus it has become a tradition.’”
